data.narrative:
nTop, a Series C robotics and manufacturing software company founded by Bradley Rothenberg and Greg Schroy, has raised $138.9M to date. Valuation analysis draws on two applicable methodologies triangulated against a comp universe of 9 private robotics and manufacturing firms at similar or adjacent stages, plus 1 public comparable.

Stage-progression analysis, using total capital raised as a proxy baseline, applies a 1.7x multiplier typical for Series C advancement, yielding $236M. Peer-median analysis across 7 same-sector comparables—including Exotec ($2.0B, Series D), Generalist AI ($2.0B, Series B), Bedrock Robotics ($1.8B, Series B), Dexterity ($1.6B, Series B), and Hadrian ($1.6B, Series D)—produces a median valuation of $1.6B, with a range of $1.0B to $2.0B. The divergence between methods reflects stage heterogeneity within the peer set.

The triangulated analysis implies a valuation range of $201M (low) to $1.9B (high), with a median of $943M. The wide dispersion underscores two key uncertainties: whether nTop's metrics and market position align more closely with earlier-stage ($1.6B median) or growth-stage peers, and the degree to which Series C positioning supports step-up multiples versus peer-based anchoring. Reconciliation would benefit from clarity on revenue, margin profile, and customer concentration relative to the named comparables.
